item.title: "Farcical trial by kangaroo court": BCL President slams Bangladesh ICT verdict on Sheikh Hasina
item.description: President Saddam Hussain on Wednesday slammed the verdict delivered by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, describing the proceedings as a ...
item.content:encoded:
"Farcical trial by kangaroo court": BCL President slams Bangladesh ICT verdict on Sheikh Hasina Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL) President Saddam Hussain on Wednesday slammed the verdict delivered by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, describing the proceedings as a "farcical trial by the kangaroo court" and alleging that they were unconstitutional and unlawful. ANI | Updated: 25-11-2026 23:06 IST | Created: 25-11-2026 23:06 IST

Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL) President Saddam Hussain (Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL) President Saddam Hussain on Wednesday slammed the verdict delivered by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, describing the proceedings as a "farcical trial by the kangaroo court" and alleging that they were unconstitutional and unlawful. Questioning the legal proceedings against the former Prime Minister, the BCL president said that the verdict was delivered in absentia without representation from Hasina. "There is a farcical trial by the kangaroo court, and it is totally unconstitutional and unlawful. It is against the international legal systems and justice systems, because the verdict was given in absentia. There was no counsel from the Awami League president, Sheikh Hasina," he said. Hussain further said that Hasina was prepared to challenge the proceedings through legal and political means. "But she also said that she is ready to face it legally and politically, and she is ready to face the injustice and the gross human rights violation challenges and try to do her best for restoring human rights, democratic systems, and an independent judiciary," he added. Speaking on Hasina's proposed return to Bangladesh by December 16, Hussain expressed support, claiming that people in the country were waiting to welcome her back. "Sheikh Hasina already declared that she wanted to go back to Bangladesh by 16 December, and the people of Bangladesh are waiting for her; they are ready to welcome her, because without the comeback of Sheikh Hasina, it is not possible to restore democracy, human rights, justice, and inclusive politics. So she has already declared the date and also taken necessary steps in diplomatic channels," Hussain said. Hasina's proposed return has also drawn a strong response from Bangladesh's current administration. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir on Tuesday said the former Prime Minister would only be allowed to return as a prisoner through extradition, dismissing reports of her planned December 16 return from India. "The reality is that a terrorist will never be allowed to return except through extradition. She is not a regular commercial passenger. She can only be brought back in handcuffs and under strict surveillance," Kobir was quoted as saying by Bangladesh Daily, The Business Standard. Hasina's spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, had earlier said that the former Prime Minister had sought arrangements from the Dhaka administration to travel from Delhi to Dhaka aboard Biman Bangladesh Airlines on December 16, coinciding with Bangladesh's Victory Day. "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," Ali said, according to Reuters. Hasina, who served as Bangladesh's Prime Minister from 2009 to 2024, arrived in India on August 5, 2024, following a student-led agitation that escalated into a nationwide uprising against her government. Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal subsequently sentenced her to death in absentia over charges of crimes against humanity linked to the suppression of protesters, allegations that Hasina has denied. Dhaka has repeatedly sought her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that the request is being examined in accordance with established processes. (ANI)

item.title: US proposes up to 25% tariff on Indian goods, may lower it to 17% if trade agreement is reached
item.description: The United States Trade Representative (USTR) on Wednesday proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, with certain exemptions, while indicating that the rate could be lowered to 17 per ...
item.content:encoded:
US proposes up to 25% tariff on Indian goods, may lower it to 17% if trade agreement is reached The United States Trade Representative (USTR) on Wednesday proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, with certain exemptions, while indicating that the rate could be lowered to 17 per cent if India reaches an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with Washington that addresses the findings of its investigation into structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors. ANI | Updated: 25-11-2026 20:12 IST | Created: 25-11-2026 20:12 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States Trade Representative (USTR) on Wednesday proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, with certain exemptions, while indicating that the rate could be lowered to 17 per cent if India reaches an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with Washington that addresses the findings of its investigation into structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors. "The Trade Representative proposes that appropriate action to obtain the elimination of the acts, policies, and practices would include applying tariffs of up to 25 percent on all goods of India, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods," the USTR said in an official statement. The USTR further proposed considering adjustments to the additional duties to account for tariffs imposed under existing Section 301 and Section 232 actions, or a tariff rate of 17 per cent if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement addressing the findings of the investigation. The announcement comes after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer determined that the acts, policies and practices of 14 economies, including India, relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors are unreasonable and burden or restrict US commerce. Among other trading partners, the USTR proposed tariffs of up to 35 per cent on Vietnam, 20 per cent on China and Singapore, and 18 per cent on Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand. Tariffs of up to 15 per cent, net of Most Favoured Nation (MFN) rates and existing Section 301 duties, have been proposed for the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan. The USTR also proposed considering lower tariff rates of 20 per cent for Vietnam and 10 per cent for Singapore, subject to trade agreements or commitments addressing the findings of the respective investigations. With respect to India, the USTR flagged industrial plans to expand manufacturing, inadequate labour protections, financial repression policies, sustained market access barriers and an alleged failure to address global excess capacity and production, including through imports and foreign direct investment from non-market economies. The USTR alleged that these practices reduce commercial opportunities for US producers and exporters in India and third-country markets, contribute to losses in production, exports, jobs and investment in US manufacturing, and increase US economic security risks. "This is especially true in sectors like health (pharmaceuticals and medical devices), steel, solar, and information and communications technology (ICT)," the statement said. The USTR has invited public comments on the proposed tariff measures, with written submissions and requests to appear at the hearings due by January 5, 2027. The hearings are scheduled to commence on January 25, 2027. The investigations were initiated on March 11, 2026, under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, covering 16 economies, including India, China, Japan and the European Union. Earlier on November 15, Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that Washington had assured New Delhi of preferential trade access with lower duties than its competing countries. "India will get preferential trade access in the US with lower duty than our competitor countries," Goyal had said while addressing the media in Cairo, Egypt. The minister had further highlighted that the commitment formed part of a broad framework agreement reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump. "This was already agreed between the leaders, President Trump and Prime Minister Modi, when they announced that we have both come to a broad framework agreement a few months ago," Goyal had said. (ANI)

item.title: Voluntary return to her country separate matter from extradition request: MEA on Sheikh Hasina's Bangladesh return plans
item.description: The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Wednesday said that Sheikh Hasina's willingness to voluntarily return to Bangladesh on a travel document would be a separate matter from the extradition ...
item.content:encoded:
Voluntary return to her country separate matter from extradition request: MEA on Sheikh Hasina's Bangladesh return plans The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Wednesday said that Sheikh Hasina's willingness to voluntarily return to Bangladesh on a travel document would be a separate matter from the extradition request made by Dhaka, reiterating that the request is being examined in accordance with established procedures. ANI | Updated: 25-11-2026 19:50 IST | Created: 25-11-2026 19:50 IST

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal (Photo/Youtube@Ministry of External Affairs, India). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Wednesday said that Sheikh Hasina's willingness to voluntarily return to Bangladesh on a travel document would be a separate matter from the extradition request made by Dhaka, reiterating that the request is being examined in accordance with established procedures. Responding to a question regarding Bangladesh's extradition request for Hasina during a media briefing here, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the matter was under examination while distinguishing it from any possible voluntary return by Hasina. "The extradition request, as I've said this before, is being examined in line with our established processes. The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition request," Jaiswal said. The MEA's remarks come amid reports that Hasina intends to return to Bangladesh on December 16, coinciding with the country's Victory Day celebrations. Her spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, reportedly said earlier that she had sought arrangements from the Dhaka administration to travel from Delhi to Dhaka aboard the national flag carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines. "Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," Ali said, according to Reuters. However, Bangladesh's State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Humayun Kobir, on Tuesday dismissed the reported plan, stating that Hasina would only be allowed to return through extradition and under custody. "The reality is that a terrorist will never be allowed to return except through extradition... She is not a regular commercial passenger. She can only be brought back in handcuffs and under strict surveillance," Bangladesh Daily, The Business Standard quoted Kobir as saying. Kobir also reportedly described Hasina's request as delusional, while the chief prosecutor of Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) termed her appeal for a state aircraft to bring her back as "nothing but madness". Meanwhile, during the same briefing, the MEA also expressed concern over reports of violence against minorities in Bangladesh and urged the country's government to investigate the incidents and bring those responsible to justice. Responding to a question about reported attacks on Hindus in areas including Narail and Pabna, Jaiswal said, "We understandably are concerned at the incidents of violence against minorities in Bangladesh. We urge the government of Bangladesh to thoroughly investigate these incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice." Hasina, who served as Bangladesh's Prime Minister from 2009 until 2024, arrived in India on August 5, 2024, following a student-led uprising over public sector job quotas that escalated into a nationwide unrest against her government. She was subsequently sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal over charges of crimes against humanity linked to the suppression of protesters, allegations that she has denied. Dhaka has repeatedly sought her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that the request is being examined through its established processes. (ANI)

item.title: US GDP growth revised sharply upwards to 4.3% in third quarter
item.description: The US economy grew at an annualised rate of 4.3 per cent in the July-September quarter of 2026, revised sharply upwards from 3.4 per cent, driven by stronger investment and consumer spending, ...
item.content:encoded:
US GDP growth revised sharply upwards to 4.3% in third quarter The US economy grew at an annualised rate of 4.3 per cent in the July-September quarter of 2026, revised sharply upwards from 3.4 per cent, driven by stronger investment and consumer spending, according to data released by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on Wednesday. ANI | Updated: 25-11-2026 19:30 IST | Created: 25-11-2026 19:30 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The US economy grew at an annualised rate of 4.3 per cent in the July-September quarter of 2026, revised sharply upwards from 3.4 per cent, driven by stronger investment and consumer spending, according to data released by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on Wednesday. Economic growth nearly doubled from 2.2 per cent recorded in the preceding April-June quarter. "Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending," the BEA said. The expansion in economic activity during the third quarter was supported by increases in investment, consumer spending and government expenditure, which were partly offset by a decline in exports. Imports also increased during the quarter. "Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports," the BEA said. Domestic demand also remained strong during the quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, which comprise consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased by 5.8 per cent. The upward revision in investment was primarily led by intellectual property products, particularly software, while the revision in consumer spending was driven by higher expenditure on goods, including pharmaceuticals, computer software and accessories, and gasoline and other energy products. On the inflation front, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation indicator monitored by the US Federal Reserve, increased by 2.1 per cent during the quarter. Core PCE inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, stood at 2.5 per cent, while the gross domestic purchases price index increased by 2.7 per cent. Real gross domestic income (GDI), another measure of economic activity, increased by 4.4 per cent in the third quarter, compared with 2.3 per cent in the preceding quarter. However, the increase in corporate profits moderated despite the acceleration in economic growth. "Profits from current production (corporate profits with inventory valuation and capital consumption adjustments) increased $206.0 billion in the third quarter, compared with an increase of $384.0 billion in the second quarter," the BEA said. On a non-annualised quarterly basis, the US economy expanded by 1.1 per cent during July-September. (ANI)
